An overview of this role 
 As an Executive Assistant at GitLab, you’ll help two senior leaders protect time for their priorities. You’ll primarily support a Vice President in Product and also support a Vice President in Marketing. You’ll manage both executives’ calendars, travel, and expenses.
 This all-remote role is open to candidates in the United States and Canada, with no preference for a specific time zone within those countries.
 What you’ll do 
 Manage both executives’ calendars across time zones, resolving scheduling conflicts before they disrupt priority meetings.
 Prepare a complete itinerary for each domestic or international trip, including flights, hotels, and any required visas.
 Submit and reconcile expense reports for both executives by each reporting deadline, following GitLab’s travel and expense policies.
 Coordinate recurring leadership activities with the Senior Executive Business Partner and keep shared office resources, distribution lists, Slack channels, and calendars up to date.
 Plan team events, offsites, and large meetings with partners across GitLab so schedules and logistics are in place before each event.
 Use artificial intelligence (AI) tools like Claude to capture meeting notes and reduce manual note-taking while protecting confidential information.
 Cover for other Executive Business Administrators by handling time-sensitive calendar, travel, and expense requests before they’re due.
 What you’ll bring 
 Experience providing executive-level administrative support to multiple senior leaders at once and adapting to each leader’s needs.
 Proficiency with productivity, video meeting, team messaging, and travel and expense tools, and the ability to learn new tools quickly. We use Google Workspace, Zoom, Slack, and Navan. Experience with comparable tools, such as Microsoft Teams for messaging, is welcome.
 Sound judgment under pressure: you can work independently, stay composed when plans change, and know when to reprioritize or escalate competing executive requests.
 Experience planning offsites or comparable events, with the organization, clear communication, and attention to detail to coordinate with multiple teams.
 Experience using AI to improve day-to-day operations while keeping sensitive information confidential.
 Ability to build relationships and gather context remotely, with flexibility in your working hours to coordinate across regions. Experience supporting teams across offices or regions can transfer to this role.
 Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally to support executives, offsites, and key events. Expect roughly one trip per quarter on average, though frequency will vary.
 Experience supporting Product or Design leaders, or working at a software company or startup, is helpful but not required.
 We welcome candidates from different backgrounds and value transferable experience.
 About the team 
 The Executive Business Administration team helps GitLab’s leaders work effectively in an asynchronous environment. We work with teams across GitLab to coordinate leadership meetings, maintain shared resources, and bring people together for events. You’ll partner with our Senior Executive Business Partner and other Executive Business Administrators.
 How GitLab will support you 
 Flexible Paid Time Off 
 Team Member Resource Groups 
 Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan 
 Growth and Development Fund 
 Parental leave 
 Home office support

Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. Denison is looking to hire a Wellfield Supervisor – Operations to support work at its Wheeler River Project. Reporting to the Denison Wellfield Manager, the primary responsibility of the  Wellfield Supervisor is to assist in coordinating personnel, equipment and procedures to ensure safe and efficient execution of drilling operations. Additional responsibilities include managing daily rig activities, enforcing strict health and safety (HSE) standards, responding to incidents and maintain regulatory compliance, addressing downhole problems, equipment failures or delays quickly and liaising with office base support teams.
 YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Supervise and coordinate drilling operations in alignment with safety and efficiency targets
 Liaise with rig crew, operators, and third-party service providers to ensure smooth execution
 Monitor wellbore progress, rig performance, and contractor deliverables
 Oversee operation of permeability enhancement and stimulation tools for production wells
 Provide leadership on site and resolve operational issues proactively
 Maintain detailed drilling records and ensure compliance with HSE and company policies
 Recommend process improvements and technical solutions as needed
 Crew Management: Lead and manage drilling crews, providing guidance, training, and development opportunities
 Ensure proper maintenance of drilling equipment, conducting regular inspections and maintenance are being upheld
 The position is based at Denison’s Wheeler River Project site, working on a 2-week on / 2-week off rotation. The successful candidate will be responsible for arranging their own travel to a designated pick-up point near Denison’s Saskatoon office or enroute to the Project site. Denison will provide board and lodging during all work rotations.
 We are seeking an experienced  Wellfield Supervisor  to oversee day-to-day operations for our upcoming ISR mining drilling operations, including the development of freeze holes and production wells. This role is ideal for a seasoned individual with proven operational expertise and a strong network across the drilling/completion spectrum. The ideal candidate is well-rounded, committed to Health and Safety in the workplace, good organizational skills, a strong sense of responsibility and demonstrated ability to work well in a team environment. In addition, the successful candidate will have: 
 10+ years' experience in drilling/completions operations (Land or Offshore)
 Prior experience as a (WSS) Wellsite Supervisor, Company Man, or drilling/service rig background
 Experience in a broad range of drilling methodologies including diamond core, mud rotary and service rigs
 Strong understanding of rig equipment and drilling fluids 
 Able to work rotational schedules in remote locations
 Strong communication skills are essential
 Experience with Pason/NOV/Rig manager or another form of Electronic Drilling Recorder (EDR)
 Previous relevant work experience (e.g., in uranium, mining industry, Oil & Gas)
 Experience with Microsoft Office and Excel
 First Aid Certification must be valid at time of hire, or willingness to become certified prior to commencing employment. 
 Willingness and ability to work on a 2-week rotation in a remote mining camp in northern Saskatchewan
 Previous work experience in a remote location is considered an asset
 Valid class 5 driver’s license (advise if missing)
 All applicants must be eligible to work in Canada. Denison offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including health and dental coverage, and a retirement savings plan.

Trace la courbe de ta carrière dans notre équipe Investissement Québec 
 Choisir Investissement Québec, c’est devenir le partenaire de milliers d’entreprises québécoises et les accompagner dans la réalisation de leurs plus grandes ambitions. C’est aussi tracer la courbe de ta carrière avec une équipe fière et engagée.
 Votre rôle : 
 Investissement Québec se dote d’un Bureau de l’intelligence artificielle afin de coordonner la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie IA et de sa gouvernance, et de favoriser une adoption structurée, responsable et alignée sur les besoins de l’organisation. En collaboration étroite avec les secteurs, les fonctions expertes et les équipes des technologies de l’information, le Bureau accompagne l’analyse, l’expérimentation et l’adoption des initiatives, dans le respect des responsabilités de chacun.
 Dans ce contexte, le conseiller principal définit, met en œuvre et fait évoluer la gouvernance, les processus et les pratiques de gestion du portefeuille d’initiatives IA. Il conseille le directeur du Bureau de l’intelligence artificielle et soutient les initiatives, tout au long de leur cycle de vie, de la définition du besoin à l’évaluation des résultats.
 Il assure une vue intégrée du portefeuille, le suivi des indicateurs, la qualité de l’information décisionnelle et la traçabilité des décisions. Il exerce une autorité fonctionnelle quant à l’application des processus de gouvernance et des critères de passage, tandis que les décisions relatives aux orientations, aux investissements, aux priorités et à l’acceptation des risques relèvent des instances habilitées.
 Il assure l’application de la gouvernance du portefeuille IA, soutient la prise de décision, coordonne le suivi des dossiers et contribue à la gestion des risques afin d’optimiser la valeur du portefeuille. Par son rôle transversal, il assure une utilisation responsable de l’IA, alignée sur les priorités de la Société.
 Vos responsabilités principales : 
 Gouvernance et processus 
 Définir, mettre en œuvre et faire évoluer la gouvernance des initiatives IA, notamment les rôles et responsabilités, les niveaux d’autorité, les critères de passage et les mécanismes d’escalade, etc., afin d’assurer un encadrement cohérent, proportionné aux risques et adapté à la maturité de l’organisation.
 Structurer et améliorer les processus liés au cycle de vie des initiatives IA, de la réception des demandes jusqu’au suivi des résultats, incluant l’expérimentation et la collecte des indicateurs. Maintenir les gabarits, registres et outils nécessaires à leur application.
 Exercer l’autorité fonctionnelle prévue aux processus de gouvernance, valider la conformité et la complétude des dossiers, demander les correctifs requis et autoriser leur cheminement vers les instances appropriées.
 Pilotage du portefeuille et information décisionnelle 
 Piloter le portefeuille des initiatives IA, et assurer une vue intégrée des priorités, des ressources, des coûts, des prévisions, des dépendances, des risques et des bénéfices attendus. Analyser les écarts et recommander les ajustements requis pour soutenir les décisions d’investissement, de priorisation et d’allocation des ressources.
 Définir, consolider et suivre les indicateurs clés de performance liée notamment à la valeur, à l’adoption, à l’avancement, à la capacité, aux risques et à la conformité afin de soutenir la reddition de comptes à la prise de décision.
 Préparer les dossiers décisionnels, les recommandations et les présentations destinés aux comités et aux instances de gouvernance. Assurer la traçabilité des décisions, des risques, des conditions d’usage et des engagements, et coordonner les suivis requis . 
 Expérimentations et projets pilotes 
 Mettre en place et encadrer les bancs d’essai, les expérimentations et les projets pilotes IA en établissant leur cadre de réalisation, leurs objectifs, leurs critères de succès et leurs indicateurs. Mobiliser les parties prenantes, analyser les résultats et recommander la poursuite, l’ajustement, le déploiement à plus grande échelle ou l’arrêt des initiatives.
 Conseil stratégique et évolution des pratiques 
 Agir comme expert-conseil auprès du directeur et des parties prenantes en faisant ressortir les enjeux transversaux, les dépendances et les arbitrages requis, et en formulant des recommandations claires visant à soutenir la prise de décision.
 Faire progresser la maturité organisationnelle en IA en évaluant les pratiques, les capacités et les mécanismes en place, en ciblant les écarts et en proposant une trajectoire d’évolution. Adapter la gouvernance afin qu’elle demeure applicable, efficace et proportionnée aux risques.
 Assurer une veille et soutenir l’amélioration continue en analysant les cadres, les normes et les meilleures pratiques en gouvernance et en gestion de portefeuille IA, puis en traduisant les apprentissages en améliorations concrètes. Repérer les besoins communs, les cas d’usage apparentés et les actifs réutilisables afin d’éviter les dédoublements.
 Vos qualifications spécifiques requises : 
 Baccalauréat en administration, gestion, systèmes d’information, technologies, transformation organisationnelle ou dans un domaine pertinent.
 Huit (8) années d’expérience pertinente, dont au moins quatre (4) dans un rôle d’expertise en conseil, en gouvernance, en gestion de portefeuille, en transformation ou en gestion d’initiatives complexes.
 Bonne connaissance des enjeux liés au numérique, aux données et à l’IA : valeur, adoption, gouvernance, risques et usage responsable.
 Expertise démontrée en gouvernance, en processus transversaux et en pilotage de portefeuille, ainsi que dans l’adaptation de cadres, de normes et de meilleures pratiques au contexte organisationnel.
 Expérience en priorisation, arbitrage, gestion des risques, suivi financier et suivi d’indicateurs de performance.
 Expérience dans la mise en place, l’encadrement et le suivi de bancs d’essai, d’expérimentations ou de projets pilotes, incluant la définition de critères de succès, l’analyse des résultats et la formulation de recommandations.
 Expérience dans la préparation de recommandations, de tableaux de bord et de dossiers destinés à la direction ou à des comités.
 Capacité démontrée à influencer, à mobiliser et à orienter les travaux sans autorité hiérarchique.
 Expérience dans une organisation complexe ou réglementée, un atout.
 Certification pertinente en gouvernance, portefeuille, programmes, projets ou processus, un atout.
 Profil général recherché : 
 Fait preuve d’un excellent jugement et formule des recommandations claires dans des situations complexes ou ambiguës.
 Exerce un leadership transversal et mobilise des parties prenantes de différents niveaux autour d’objectifs communs.
 Possède une vision d’ensemble et relie les enjeux de gouvernance, de risques, de coûts, de capacités et de valeur.
 Démontre une grande capacité d’analyse, de synthèse et de priorisation.
 Communique avec clarté, rigueur et sens politique auprès des lignes d’affaires, des experts, de la direction et des comités.
 Travaille avec autonomie, rigueur et méthode, en assurant la traçabilité des travaux et la cohérence organisationnelle.
 Fait preuve d’agilité, de curiosité et d’une forte orientation vers les résultats et l’amélioration continue.

 Evaluating requests using Ontario Human Rights Commission principles, institutional policies, and relevant case law

What is The Role 
 The Context Engine team builds the knowledge layer that AI agents use to work with enterprise data in Elasticsearch. We extract knowledge from any data sources into a structured AI Index, serve it to agents through public APIs, MCP tools and framework integrations, and close the loop with agent traces so that what the engine knows improves from real usage. Any agent can use it: Elastic’s own Agent Builder, Claude Code, LangChain and other third-party harnesses.
 As a Principal AI Engineer, you own the improvement loop of this product end to end: how agents, automations and skills behave in production, how we observe them, how we evaluate them, and how we ship changes to them safely. This is a hybrid role at the intersection of engineering, data science, and product. You will write production code, design evaluation and telemetry that product decisions can rest on, and set the technical bar for how the team iterates on agentic behaviour. You will work alongside data scientists, backend engineers, product, and UX, and your work will show up directly in what customers build on top of Elastic.
 The codebase is TypeScript and we build it in the open, so you'll be shipping code, designs and discussions in public alongside the rest of the Elastic Stack.
 What You Will Be Doing 
 Own the production improvement loop for Context Engine: understand how extraction automations, retrieval tools and memory behave, based on offline evaluations and customer conversations and telemetry. You help find the failure modes, fix them, and prove the fix.
 Define how we iterate on agents and skills safely: versioning and rollout of prompts, skills and automations, regression coverage, staged and shadow evaluation, and the guardrails that let us change behaviour without breaking customers.
 Design the telemetry we need to make data-informed engineering decisions: what to capture from agent traces, tool calls and knowledge retrieval, how it lands in Elasticsearch, and how it feeds evaluation, dashboards and the feedback loop.
 Partner with the data science team on evaluation strategy: golden datasets, evaluators to gate on quality, latency and cost.
 Raise the bar across the team: review designs and PRs, mentor engineers in eval-driven development, and write the technical proposals that shape the roadmap.
 What You Bring
 10+ years of software engineering experience, with the recent years spent shipping and operating AI-driven products on real production traffic, ideally products with public APIs and data models that had to evolve without breaking customers.
 A track record of eval-driven product improvement: you have diagnosed agent or LLM behaviour from traces and user feedback, designed the evaluation that exposed the problem, shipped the fix and measured the outcome.
 Direct experience building agents with state and memory, and iterating on prompts, skills and tool behaviour safely in production.
 You can explain how tool calls and their results flow through each iteration, how context grows across turns and how you manage it, and how the loop decides to stop.
 Familiarity with MCP, including exposing public MCP servers and tools.
 Experience designing telemetry for AI systems, and using it to make engineering and product decisions.
 Experience running product experiments end to end: instrumentation, unattended execution, and interpreting results.
 Experience building products with public APIs and evolving data models, and the judgement that comes with maintaining external contracts as a product changes.
 Strong backend engineering skills in either Python or TypeScript: APIs, stateful workflows, data pipelines and production services.

 As the Information Security Specialist responsible for PCI compliance, you will:
 Own the PCI compliance program 
 Maintain end-to-end accountability for PCI compliance across the TD Insurance family, from annual planning and scope validation through evidence submission, assessment support, remediation, attestation, and ongoing compliance.
 Establish and maintain the annual PCI compliance roadmap, milestones, deliverables, ownership model, and governance calendar.
 Translate PCI DSS requirements into clear obligations for business, application, infrastructure, security, operations, and third-party teams.
 Act as the primary TD Insurance PCI subject-matter expert and central point of coordination for internal stakeholders and external assessors.
 Maintain scope and control accountability 
 Lead the annual confirmation of the cardholder data environment, including payment channels, applications, infrastructure, data flows, integrations, service providers, and connected systems.
 Maintain the PCI system inventory, data-flow diagrams, scope rationale, control-owner register, responsibility matrix, evidence catalogue, and applicability decisions.
 Challenge unnecessary scope and identify sustainable scope-reduction opportunities through segmentation, tokenization, outsourcing, architectural change, or removal of cardholder data.
 Ensure control responsibilities are clearly assigned across all applicable PCI requirements and that accountable owners understand their ongoing obligations.
 Drive assessments and evidence readiness 
 Coordinate annual PCI DSS assessments and associated deliverables, including the applicable Report on Compliance, Self-Assessment Questionnaire, and Attestation of Compliance.
 Partner with Qualified Security Assessors, Approved Scanning Vendors, internal audit, cyber security, compliance, and control owners throughout the assessment lifecycle.
 Implement a disciplined evidence-management process that confirms evidence is complete, current, accurate, approved, traceable, and assessment-ready.
 Conduct readiness reviews and control-health assessments before formal testing begins.
 Maintain a defensible record of scope determinations, control design decisions, exceptions, targeted risk analyses, and compensating controls.
 PCI DSS v4.0.1 is the current standard identified in the PCI Security Standards Council document library, which also provides the prioritized approach, assessment templates, attestations, targeted-risk-analysis material, and guidance for compensating controls.
 Deliver compliance outcomes 
 Track PCI deliverables, control gaps, evidence deficiencies, risks, dependencies, and remediation commitments from identification through validated closure.
 Develop practical remediation plans with named owners, target dates, interim controls, dependencies, and measurable closure criteria.
 Escalate overdue or ineffective remediation promptly, clearly articulating customer, business, technology, compliance, and reputational impacts.
 Coordinate the resources and decisions required to meet assessment deadlines, rather than limiting the role to status reporting.
 Verify that remediation addresses the underlying control weakness and produces sustainable evidence for future assessments.
 Identify recurring issues and implement processes, control, automation, or governance improvements to prevent repeat findings.

 Escalate material control deficiencies through the appropriate technology, risk, compliance, and business governance channels.
 Embed continuous compliance 
 Move the program from annual assessment preparation toward continuous compliance and year-round control ownership.
 Establish recurring checkpoints for control validation, evidence refresh, vulnerability management, access reviews, penetration testing, external scans, incident-response exercises, third-party monitoring, and policy reviews.

 Develop reusable templates, procedures, playbooks, training materials, and evidence standards to improve consistency and reduce key-person dependency.

 Direct, hands-on experience owning or leading a PCI DSS compliance program or a substantial PCI workstream through a complete assessment lifecycle.

Anticiper. Planifier. Donner le rythme à nos projets.

 L'équipe derrière le génie 
 Chez Norda Stelo, nous croyons que les grands projets méritent une vision à la hauteur de leurs ambitions. Notre Bureau de gestion de projet accompagne les organisations dans la réalisation de projets de toutes envergures, de la planification stratégique jusqu'à leur livraison. Présent dans des secteurs aussi variés que les mines, l'énergie, les infrastructures et l'industrie, il joue un rôle transversal auprès de l'ensemble de l'organisation. 
 Le Bureau de gestion de projet contribue à la réussite des ventes et des projets de Norda Stelo, de la préparation de l'offre de service à la réalisation des mandats. Nous travaillons avec les équipes de vente, les responsables de projet et les centres d'excellence pour que nos experts se concentrent sur ce qu'ils font de mieux. 
 Notre raison d'être 
 Soutenir la réussite des ventes et des projets de Norda Stelo : contribuer à des offres de service solides et compétitives, puis à une réalisation rigoureuse et performante des mandats. Nous faisons évoluer nos pratiques pour mieux saisir les occasions d’affaires et anticiper les risques. 
 Ce qui nous définit 
 · Le soutien aux ventes. Avec les équipes de vente et les experts, nous valorisons nos expertises et nos réalisations dans les offres de service. Nos propositions répondent aux besoins des clients et se démarquent par leur qualité. 
 · Le soutien aux projets. Nous appuyons les responsables de projet avec le contrôle des coûts, les agents de projet, le contrôle documentaire, la formation et le suivi des risques. 
 · La transformation opérationnelle. Nous faisons évoluer nos processus, nos outils et nos mesures de performance, avec une gouvernance claire, pour améliorer en continu notre façon de gérer les projets. 
 Notre façon de travailler 
 Nous accompagnons chaque projet de bout en bout, de l'offre de service à la clôture. Nous croyons à l'intelligence collective et à la collaboration, avec les valeurs de Norda Stelo : confiance, excellence, intégrité, respect, innovation et adaptabilité. 
 Notre ambition 
 Être le partenaire privilégié de nos équipes de vente et de projet : des offres de service mieux préparées pour remporter des mandats rentables, et des projets mieux soutenus pour les livrer avec confiance. 
 Votre rôle : influencer, anticiper et faire évoluer 
 Relevant de la Directrice du Bureau de gestion de projet, vous agirez comme une référence en planification et en contrôle des échéanciers. Vous accompagnerez les directeurs et les équipes de projets dans l'élaboration de stratégies de planification robustes, la maîtrise des échéanciers et l'anticipation des risques.

 Élaborer les stratégies de planification : développer des échéanciers directeurs et détaillés pour les différentes phases des projets, de l'ingénierie à l'approvisionnement, la construction et la mise en service.
 Structurer et optimiser les échéanciers : établir les séquences d'activités, les interdépendances, les jalons clés, les chemins critiques et les besoins en ressources.
 Assurer le suivi de la performance : analyser l'avancement réel par rapport aux échéanciers de référence, mesurer les écarts et produire des prévisions fiables.

 Conseiller les équipes de projets : accompagner les directeurs et responsables de projets dans leurs décisions, les stratégies de rattrapage et l'optimisation des échéanciers.
 Produire des analyses et des rapports de gestion : préparer les tableaux de bord, les rapports d'avancement et les indicateurs de performance afin de soutenir la prise de décision.

 10 ans et plus d'expérience en planification et contrôle d'échéanciers dans un environnement de projets complexes.

 Leadership, autonomie, rigueur et excellentes habiletés de communication et de collaboration.
 Bilinguisme français et anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit, afin de collaborer avec des équipes et des clients au Canada et à l'international.
 Pourquoi choisir Norda Stelo? 
 Parce qu'ici, votre expertise peut avoir un impact bien au-delà de votre rôle !

 Une carrière à long terme : un poste permanent au sein d'une firme en croissance qui valorise l'initiative et l'expertise. 
 Une culture sérieusement humaine : un milieu où la collaboration, la transparence, l'autonomie et la reconnaissance font partie de notre quotidien.

 Suivez votre étoile et joignez-vous à une équipe où votre expertise compte, vos idées font avancer les choses et votre contribution génère de l'ingénierie d'impact!

 Job Description 
 At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. We provide our teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while taking science a step beyond through research, development and delivery of life-changing therapies.  Must be legally authorized to work in the United States or Canada without sponsorship.

 Must be able to work with regular overlap to support China working hours.
 Position Summary:
 Thermo Fisher Scientific is seeking a physician with extensive oncology clinical development experience to join a cross-functional team that identifies, evaluates, and partners with biotechnology companies and academic laboratories in China that are developing novel oncology therapeutics. Many of these programs generate promising preclinical and early-phase clinical data in China but have not yet established the regulatory, operational, and strategic foundation required to advance into multiregional trials and global registration.
 The incumbent will evaluate preclinical and clinical-stage oncology assets, assess which are most likely to succeed in global development, and help shape partnerships through which Thermo Fisher Scientific and its PPD clinical research business support these assets in their transition from early-phase trials in China to global pivotal trials and registration with regulators such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA).
 As a member of a larger diligence team, the incumbent will provide the medical and scientific judgment that underpins strategic recommendations to Thermo Fisher Scientific senior leadership as to which assets and companies should be prioritized and which should be deprioritized. The position requires proven ability to drive both strategic and measurable business outcomes. The incumbent’s oncology track record and expertise must be extensive enough to ensure recognition as a peer of senior medical and scientific leaders in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries.
 Key Responsibilities:
 1. Asset Identification and Scientific Due Diligence
 Identify and screen preclinical and clinical-stage oncology assets originating from biotechnology companies, academic laboratories, and research hospitals in China, drawing on scientific literature, conference presentations, regulatory and trial registry records, and direct engagement with sponsors and investigators.
 Evaluate the scientific foundation of each asset, including mechanism of action, target validation, biological rationale, preclinical pharmacology and toxicology, and translational and biomarker strategy.
 Assess differentiation relative to current standard of care and to competing assets in development globally, across modalities including antibody–drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, cell and gene therapies, and targeted small molecules.
 Critically appraise early-phase clinical data generated in China, including dose-escalation design, dose selection and optimization, safety and tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy, with attention to study design quality, endpoint selection, data integrity, and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance.
 Assess the likely applicability of China-generated clinical data to global regulatory submissions, taking into account differences in standard of care, patient populations, and trial conduct, with reference to International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines E5 (ethnic factors in the acceptability of foreign clinical data) and E17 (multiregional clinical trials) and to FDA regulations and guidance on the use of foreign clinical data.
 Define the remaining path to global registration for each asset, including indication and line-of-therapy selection, likely regulatory expectations in the United States, European Union, and other major markets, and the principal clinical, regulatory, and technical risks.
 Collaborate with functional experts to assess nonclinical package completeness and chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) readiness for global development.
 2. Strategic Recommendations and Portfolio Prioritization
 Synthesize scientific, clinical, regulatory, and commercial findings into clear, evidence-based recommendations on whether each asset and company should be prioritized, monitored, or deprioritized.
 Contribute to the development and consistent application of a structured evaluation framework and scoring criteria that allow assets to be compared across modalities, tumor types, and stages of development.
 Prepare and present diligence findings and recommendations to Thermo Fisher Scientific senior leadership and governance forums, communicating complex scientific information concisely to executive audiences.
 Monitor the oncology innovation landscape in China, the cross-border licensing and partnering environment, and relevant regulatory and policy developments in the United States and China, and advise leadership on their implications for portfolio strategy.
 3. Partnership Development and Global Development Strategy
 Engage peer-to-peer, in Mandarin and English, with chief medical officers, chief scientific officers, founders, and principal investigators of biotechnology companies and academic laboratories in China to build trusted relationships and support partnership discussions.
 Develop global clinical development plans for partnered assets that bridge early-phase data from China to multiregional clinical trials (MRCTs), including dose-optimization strategy, indication sequencing, registrational trial design, and endpoint selection.
 Advise partners on global regulatory strategy, including preparation for Investigational New Drug (IND) applications, pre-IND and end-of-phase meetings with FDA, scientific advice procedures with EMA, and integration of data generated under the oversight of China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) into global submissions.
 Through the PPD consulting practice, provide industry-leading product development plans and top-level design of the clinical trial protocols required by those plans.
 Support proposals, bid defenses, and client governance and advisory boards for partnered programs, including interactions with partner physicians and indication leaders.
 Author and review Investigator’s Brochures, clinical study reports, regulatory briefing documents, and clinical sections of New Drug Applications (NDAs), Biologics License Applications (BLAs), and Marketing Authorization Applications (MAAs).
 4. Cross-Functional Collaboration and Internal Expertise
 Work within a multidisciplinary diligence team that includes business development, corporate strategy, regulatory affairs, clinical operations, biostatistics, and commercial colleagues, ensuring that medical and scientific perspectives are fully integrated into recommendations.
 Liaise with investigators and key opinion leaders (KOLs) in China, the United States, and Europe to inform asset assessments and trial feasibility.
 Contribute to the design and reporting of feasibility assessments for global trials of partnered assets.
 Provide indication-specific training and guidance to internal clinical teams, and mentor and supervise clinical scientists.
 Participate in multidisciplinary working groups and initiatives that strengthen Thermo Fisher Scientific’s capabilities in supporting cross-border oncology development.

 Doctor of Medicine (MD) or equivalent required.
 Board certification, or equivalent, in medical oncology, hematology and oncology, or a closely related specialty.
 At least five years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry leading oncology clinical development, including leadership of at least one asset from discovery through registration.
 Demonstrated experience evaluating early-phase oncology data and making development or portfolio recommendations.
 Proficiency in spoken and written English and Mandarin Chinese.
 Active medical license preferred but not required.
 Preferred Qualifications:
 Direct experience with oncology programs originating in China, including clinical development under NMPA oversight or the transition of China-originated assets into global development.
 Experience conducting scientific due diligence for in-licensing, partnering, or investment decisions in a pharmaceutical business development, venture capital, or corporate strategy setting.
 Experience designing or leading MRCTs, and familiarity with the FDA Oncology Center of Excellence’s Project Optimus dose-optimization initiative and with FDA and EMA expectations for global registration.
 An established professional network among oncology investigators, biotechnology leaders, and academic institutions in China.
 Experience presenting to executive leadership teams, boards, or investment committees.
 Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
 Rigorous, independent scientific judgment, with the ability to reach clear and defensible conclusions from incomplete or heterogeneous data.
 Able to work effectively in a matrix organization.
 Able to demonstrate the following key high-performance behaviors: decisive, customer driven, flexible thinking, smart risk-taking, and continuous improvement.
 Leads, influences, and motivates staff within and across departments.
 Strong in presenting and communicating complex information clearly to scientific and executive audiences.
 Able to work effectively across Chinese and Western business and scientific cultures.
 Able to handle sensitive and confidential information, including nonpublic data from prospective partners, with discretion.
 Possesses a “can do” attitude and is capable of implementing and following through on activities and projects.
 Flexibility to travel domestically and internationally, including periodic travel to China.

 Full-time position
 Base salary plus a competitive bonus, equity, and benefits package
 Exposure to a broad portfolio of novel oncology assets across modalities and stages of development
 The opportunity to contribute to a strategic Thermo Fisher Scientific initiative supporting the global development of oncology innovation originating in China
 Compensation

 ​​One​ ​Permanent​ ​Full Time​ Position.     
 The  Sr. Analyst, Market Data  owns Capital Power’s end-to-end price curve framework within the Risk Group. The role is accountable for the quality, integrity, and governance of all price and market data curves used across the commodity portfolio, spanning new curve intake, methodology design, system configuration, daily production and validation, independent price verification (IPV), and governance reporting. 
 The successful candidate will combine strong quantitative and systems skills with sound professional judgment and a commitment to robust controls and will serve as the subject-matter expert on all matters related to commodity and market data curves.
 You will contribute to our team by: 
 Key Accountabilities: 
 • Serve as the single point of contact for all new commodity and market data curve requests and manage the intake process from request through governance approval. 
 • Design, build, calibrate, and document forward price curve models across commodities and delivery points, including directly observable, interpolated, and proxy / spread-to-benchmark approaches. 
 • Own and maintain the central curve register, ensuring all curves are catalogued with current attributes, approval status, and scheduled review dates. 
 • Configure and maintain approved price curves in ZEMA (data ingestion, quality rules, curve construction logic) and Allegro (curve definition, valuation formulas, P&L attribution); lead UAT and production deployment. 
 • Monitor daily curve production across all curves; investigate and resolve data feed failures, quality alerts, and other flags within EOD SLAs; maintain and test fallback procedures. 
 • Execute the firm's daily validation and monthly independent price verification (IPV) process; compare curve outputs to independent market sources; prepare and distribute IPV reports; escalate material exceptions. 
 • Conduct or coordinate independent validation of all new and materially modified price curve models; issue structured validation reports; track findings to remediation; manage the periodic revalidation schedule. 
 • Prepare and present submissions to Risk Oversight Committee; produce periodic governance reports covering inventory status, open findings, IPV exception trends, and curve performance. 
 • Maintain the model risk and governance framework for price curves in alignment with Model Risk Policy and applicable regulatory guidance; support audits and regulatory examinations. 
 What you will bring to the role:

 • Post-secondary degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field.
 • Advanced degree (e.g., Master’s, PhD) or professional designation (e.g., CFA, FRM, PRM) is an asset.

 • Direct experience with ZEMA and / or Allegro in a production environment strongly preferred.

 • Apply risk management systems and analytical tools (ETRM, Excel, Python, R) to build, validate, and maintain pricing models and data workflows.

 • Automate repetitive data processes and controls using scripting, with an ability to identify opportunities to streamline manual workflows.
 • Develop, validate, and maintain pricing methodologies, including proxy/spread-to-benchmark and regression-based approaches, across liquid and illiquid markets.

 POSITION SUMMARY  
 The Indigenous Patient Navigator (IPN) supports First Nations, Inuit, and Métis and Urban Indigenous patients and families to access equitable, safe, timely, and culturally responsive care across CHEO and the broader health system. Working in partnership with Indigenous patients, families, clinical teams, and community partners, The IPN facilitates navigation, advocacy, and care coordination while centering Indigenous world views, rights, and self-determination. 
 The IPN promotes the inclusion of patient and family voice in clinical decision making and supports patients and families in understanding care pathways, care plans, and follow-up. The IPN facilitates access to cultural, spiritual, emotional, and practical supports, assists with care coordination, and connects patients and families to appropriate community partners. The IPN addresses systemic barriers, responds to and supports the prevention of racism and discrimination in health care settings, and contributes to improved patient experience and health outcomes. 
 MAIN RESPONSABILITIES   
 Patient Navigation & Advocacy – 40%  
 Provide trauma informed, culturally safe navigation for Indigenous patients and families across primary, acute, specialty, and community services. 
 Support informed consent processes, care planning, appointment scheduling, referrals, discharge coordination, and follow up, including transportation and medical escort needs, where applicable. 
 Advocate for patient rights by identifying and addressing barriers (e.g., jurisdictional issues, coverage or beneﬁts, language needs, or documentation requirements) and escalating concerns related to discrimination or unsafe care. 
 Support patient and family understanding by offering explanations of diagnoses treatments options, medications, and care pathways. facilitate shared decision making throughout the patient’s care journey. 
 Participate in case management discussions or Safety Incident Report debriefs, as required. 
 Cultural Safety & Antiracism – 20%  
 Promote cultural safety practices and challenge discriminatory behaviors and policies within care environments through respectful, collaborative, and solution focused engagement. Contribute to antiracism and quality improvement initiatives. 
 Facilitate access to traditional medicines, Elders or Knowledge Keepers, ceremony (e.g., smudging), and land-based supports in alignment with patient preference and organizational policy. 
 Connect staff, medical staff, learners and volunteers to educational opportunities on Indigenous health contexts, colonial impacts, and determinants of health. 
 Contribute in partnership with Indigeneity, Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, Access, and Social Justice (I-IDEAS) to the development of educational and training resources supporting staff, medical staff, learners and volunteers on Indigenous Safer Care. 
 Documentation, Data, and Privacy – 10%  
 Document navigation activities in appropriate systems in compliance with privacy legislation and in support of Indigenous data sovereignty principles (e.g. distinction-based considerations). 
 Utilize secure, trauma informed approaches to the collection, storage, and sharing patient information, obtaining consent for the involvement of any community or external supports. 
 Contribute to program metrics (e.g., access, wait times, patient experience, cultural safety indicators) and quality improvement reporting. 
 Program & Organizational Contributions – 10%  
 Participate in case conferences, huddles, and rounds, bringing forward patient and family voice and cultural safety considerations. 
 Contribute to developing resources on available supports for medical staff beneﬁting Indigenous patients and families. 
 QUALIFICATIONS   
 Bachelor’s degree in Nursing, Social Work or a related Indigenous Health ﬁeld* (Essential) 
 Lived experience and a strong connection to Indigenous communities, including First Nations, Inuit, and Métis (Essential) 
 3 years’ experience in health navigation, case management, community health, social services, or related ﬁelds serving Indigenous peoples (Essential) 
 4 years’ experience collaborating with clinical teams and community partners (Essential) 
 Knowledge of Indigenous histories, cultures, languages, holistic wellness models, colonial impacts, intergenerational trauma, social determinants of health, community engagement, and cultural protocols (Essential) 
 Knowledge of trauma and violence informed, culturally safe, and anti-racist approaches within health systems, emphasizing choice, control, safety, strengths-based care, and reﬂective practice.

 Strong communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to translate complex clinical information, engage across cultures, and support case related discussions (Essential)

 Working knowledge of client information systems and documentation, privacy requirements, distinction-based approaches, and Indigenous data sovereignty (Essential) 
 Strong analytical, adaptability, and problem-solving skills to respond effectively to evolving patient and system needs in fast paced environments (Essential) 
 Strong organizational and time management skills to balance competing demands and priorities. 
 Commitment to excellence, patient focused care, and the consistent exercise of diplomacy and tact (Essential) 
 Training in Non-Violent Crisis Intervention Training, mediation, de-escalation, or conﬂict resolution (Preferred)

 Vulnerable Sector Check (Essential)

The Senior Product Designer owns the end-to-end user experience of Acumatica applications, shapes workflows, and aligns them with the product vision. As an active member of the discovery team, they collaborate with the Product Manager, Business Analyst, Engineering Lead, and backend developers to translate business requirements into validated, scalable solutions. This role includes building working prototypes for Business Analysts to specify from and for backend developers to connect services to, modeling system behavior, writing clear behavioral specifications for engineers and AI agents, and ensuring AI-generated output meets quality and accessibility standards. The Senior Product Designer also mentors team members, leads cross-functional design sprints, and links design work to measurable business outcomes. 
 MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Discovery & Validation: Understanding Users and Problems 
 Conduct and synthesize user research and competitive analysis, including emerging UX patterns and AI capabilities, to inform design direction 
 Validate early concepts with users through working prototypes before committing to full design or engineering effort 
 Lead usability and UX acceptance testing to ensure the experience functions as designed. Define success metrics such as task completion, error rate, CSAT, and adoption with product managers. Identify and raise UX defects before release. 
 Interactive Systems Design: Designing Behavior, Not Just Screens 
 Own end-to-end UX for assigned epics, including AI-surfaced and headless experiences. Partner with the Engineering Lead to assess feasibility and trade-offs. 
 Model user flows, screen and component states, and transitions, defining how the UI responds to user input, validation, system events, and API responses 
 Design for non-deterministic AI output by defining fallback, recovery, and human-in-the-loop behavior when results are incomplete, incorrect, or low confidence 
 Prototype & Behavioral Specification: Building the Working Reference 
 Build working code prototypes in the component library to serve as reference artifacts. These prototypes help Business Analysts write functional and business specifications and enable backend developers to connect real services. 
 Structure prototypes to be plug-in ready, with defined mock data structures and clear data shapes. Keep the UI separate from data logic to prevent backend rework. 
 Write behavioral specifications that AI coding agents can interpret clearly, covering interaction rules, states, edge cases, and UI acceptance criteria. 
 Define UI-level guardrails for AI-surfaced features, such as how uncertainty is displayed, when human confirmation is required, and how users can override. Partner with the Product Manager and Business Analyst to establish the supporting business rules. 
 Annotate prototypes with known business rules and open questions to surface rules that do not appear on screen, such as permissions, validation logic, and calculations, early in the process.

ABOUT JOBBER

The Team

Analytics sits within Jobber’s Strategy & Analytics department, Jobber’s internal consulting team and decision-support mechanism that connects data and business insight with the rest of the organization. Analytics is a central function that exists to drive business outcomes across Jobber’s ecosystem.

The Role

Jobber is looking for a Manager, Customer Analytics (Sales & Marketing) to lead the analytics function supporting our Marketing & Channels and Sales & Partnerships pods. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Customer Analytics, this leader will manage a team of analysts and partner closely with Directors, Senior Directors, and VPs across Demand Generation, Brand Marketing & Communications, Sales, Partnerships, MarketingOps, SalesOps, and Finance.

In this role, you will set the technical, methodological, and strategic direction for high-impact Sales and Marketing analytics. You will own the measurement infrastructure that helps Jobber connect acquisition investment to subscription revenue growth, understand marketing effectiveness, evaluate channel and partnership performance, and improve visibility into CAC, LTV, payback, sales efficiency, revenue funnel performance, and go-to-market ROI.

This role requires a leader who combines strong people leadership, hands-on technical depth, and deep Sales and Marketing domain expertise. You will build trusted relationships with senior leaders, raise the bar for analytical quality, and develop analysts who can translate rigorous measurement into better growth decisions.

You will also help Jobber advance Analytics 2.0 in practice by using self-serve analytics, automation, responsible AI, and agentic workflows to scale trusted decision support and create more capacity for strategic, high-judgment analytical work.

 

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Team Leadership & Analytics Operating Model

 - Hire, onboard, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of analysts supporting Demand Generation, Brand Marketing & Communications, Sales, and Partnerships, setting clear expectations and building the team’s capabilities as Jobber’s Sales and Marketing analytics needs scale.

 - Establish a clear engagement and prioritization model for Sales and Marketing Analytics, creating scalable operating rhythms that balance strategic analysis, recurring reporting, cross-functional initiatives, self-serve enablement, and ad hoc stakeholder needs.

 - Build a culture of analytical excellence, high accountability, curiosity, strong QA, documentation, peer review, business ownership, and continuous improvement.

 - Partner with Analytics Engineering, BI, Data Science, Data Engineering, MarketingOps, and SalesOps to strengthen the data foundation, metric definitions, reporting infrastructure, and governed datasets that support Sales and Marketing decision-making.

Sales & Marketing Analytics Strategy

 - Lead the analytics roadmap across Jobber’s Marketing & Channels and Sales & Partnerships pods, ensuring the team is focused on the highest-impact opportunities across customer acquisition, demand generation, sales productivity, channel performance, partnership growth, and revenue efficiency.

 - Partner with Sales and Marketing leadership to define success metrics, identify growth opportunities, evaluate strategic bets, and translate ambiguous business questions into clear analytical approaches and actionable recommendations.

 - Help Jobber understand not just what is happening across the go-to-market funnel, but why it is happening, what it means, and what leaders should do next.

Performance Marketing, Demand Generation & Channel Measurement

 - Define and evolve Jobber’s marketing measurement framework across Marketing Mix Modelling (MMM), Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA), incrementality, experimentation, and forecasting, ensuring these methods work together as a unified system for decision-making rather than as siloed tools.

 - Lead the design and operationalization of advanced marketing measurement approaches, including MMM, MTA, incrementality testing, spend efficiency curves, saturation analysis, and diminishing returns modelling, connecting marketing and channel investment to subscription revenue, CAC, payback, LTV, pipeline quality, and long-term customer value.

 - Set standards for how analysts select, build, quality-assure, and interpret advanced measurement methods, including when to use MMM, MTA, incrementality testing, causal inference, forecasting, or simpler diagnostic approaches.

 - Partner with Performance Marketing, Demand Generation, Brand Marketing & Communications, Partnerships, Finance, and MarketingOps to evaluate spend efficiency, channel mix, conversion quality, saturation, diminishing returns, and budget allocation trade-offs, including scenario analysis ahead of planning cycles.

Sales, Partnerships & Revenue Funnel Analytics

 - Lead analytics that help Sales and Partnerships leaders understand funnel health, lead quality, conversion performance, rep and team productivity, pipeline creation, sales-assisted revenue, partner/referral performance, and opportunities to improve go-to-market efficiency.

 - Build frameworks, dashboards, models, and decision-support tools that help leaders monitor performance, diagnose issues, and make better planning, resourcing, and prioritization decisions.

 - Connect sales and marketing performance into a unified view of acquisition economics, helping Jobber understand how demand, channel mix, sales motion, and customer quality translate into durable revenue growth.

Executive Influence & Storytelling

 - Bring an analytical perspective to growth strategy, planning, investment decisions, and operating reviews with Directors, Senior Directors, VPs, and cross-functional leaders.

 - Translate complex analytical work into clear narratives, trade-offs, and recommendations that senior leaders can act on.

Analytics 2.0 & AI-Powered Decision Support

 - Contribute to Jobber’s Analytics 2.0 roadmap by identifying where AI, ML, automation, and agentic analytics can accelerate Sales and Marketing measurement, forecasting, diagnostics, storytelling, and self-serve decision support.

 - Partner with Analytics Engineering, BI, Data Science, and Data Engineering to operationalize AI-assisted workflows and analytics agents for anomaly detection, campaign diagnostics, forecasting, attribution, causal inference, narrative generation, documentation, and QA.

 - Champion governed self-serve analytics and trusted metrics so Sales and Marketing leaders can answer recurring performance questions without routing every request through an analyst, while preserving analytical quality and clear ownership.

 - Help analysts adopt AI responsibly, validating outputs, understanding limitations, documenting methods, and using automation to create more capacity for strategic modelling and business influence.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

Sales & Marketing Analytics Expertise

 - Deep experience in Sales, Marketing, Growth, Revenue, Demand Generation, Performance Marketing, Channels, Partnerships, or GTM analytics, ideally in a high-growth SaaS or subscription business.

 - Strong understanding of customer acquisition economics, including CAC, LTV, payback period, funnel conversion, pipeline quality, channel performance, sales efficiency, partner/referral performance, and subscription revenue growth.

 - Deep, hands-on experience with marketing and GTM measurement approaches, including attribution, incrementality testing, experimentation, forecasting, budget allocation, and the practical limitations of each method.

 - Experience helping senior Sales and Marketing leaders define success metrics, evaluate performance, diagnose growth opportunities, and make better decisions across the go-to-market funnel.

 - Familiarity with marketing, sales, CRM, ad platform, lifecycle, partnerships, and revenue funnel data, including paid search, paid social, organic, referral, brand, partnerships, lifecycle marketing, and platform-specific measurement constraints from tools such as Google Ads, Meta, and programmatic ad platforms.

 - Hands-on experience building or significantly contributing to advanced marketing measurement approaches such as Marketing Mix Modelling, Multi-Touch Attribution, incrementality experiments, geo or matched-market tests, synthetic control, spend efficiency curves, or causal inference methods, with the judgment to evaluate, challenge, and improve vendor or platform-reported outputs.

Technical & Methodological Skills

 - Expert-level SQL skills, with the ability to work across complex data structures, build analytical datasets, and review analytical logic with confidence.

 - Strong hands-on analytical skills, including performance measurement, exploratory analysis, cohort analysis, impact evaluation, experimentation, forecasting, scenario analysis, segmentation, predictive modelling, and causal inference techniques such as difference-in-differences, synthetic control, propensity score matching, or regression discontinuity.

 - Strong proficiency in Python or R for modelling, automation, statistical analysis, and productionized analytics workflows; experience with MMM libraries or statistical modelling frameworks such as Robyn, Meridian, PyMC-Marketing, Bayesian modelling frameworks, or equivalent tools is a strong asset.

 - Strong statistical judgment, including comfort with confidence intervals, effect size estimation, variance, seasonality, bias, model uncertainty, and balancing analytical rigour with pragmatic business decision-making.

 - Experience with modern data stacks and BI tools such as dbt, Snowflake, Redshift, Looker, Tableau, or similar platforms, with a strong ability to build scalable, trusted reporting and decision-support assets.

Business & Leadership Skills

 - Proven experience as a people leader in analytics, with a strong track record of developing, coaching, and empowering high-performing analysts.

 - Strong strategic judgment, with the ability to shape priorities, influence senior leaders, and connect analytical work to company-level growth outcomes.

 - Experience owning an analytics roadmap in a fast-moving environment with competing stakeholder needs and high-impact business decisions.

 - Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trust, clarify ambiguous asks, manage trade-offs, and influence Directors, Senior Directors, VPs, and cross-functional leaders through data-backed recommendations.

 - Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis, uncertainty, and trade-offs into clear executive-ready narratives.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead AI-assisted analytics adoption across a team, including identifying high-value use cases, setting QA and governance expectations, validating outputs, improving documentation, accelerating analysis, and helping analysts use AI to deliver better decision support without compromising quality.

 

WHO YOU ARE

 - You are a strategic analytics leader who can operate at multiple altitudes. You can zoom into technical details when needed, but you always connect the work back to business decisions and outcomes.

 - You are a strong people leader who creates clarity, raises the bar, and helps analysts do the best work of their careers.

 - You are proactive and resourceful. You do not wait to be handed perfectly formed questions; you identify the highest-value problems, frame the trade-offs, and guide stakeholders toward better decisions.

 - You are deeply curious about Sales and Marketing performance. You want to understand what drives acquisition, conversion, channel effectiveness, sales efficiency, partnership growth, and long-term customer value.

 - You hold a high bar for analytical quality and measurement rigour, while staying pragmatic about what is useful, deployable, and decision-relevant in a real business environment.

 - You communicate with clarity and confidence, especially when explaining uncertainty, trade-offs, and imperfect evidence to senior stakeholders.

 - You are comfortable making trade-offs visible. You know how to say yes to the highest-impact work while helping stakeholders understand what must be deprioritized.

 - You are excited by Analytics 2.0. You see emerging tools and operating models as ways to redesign how analytics teams deliver trusted, scalable decision support, not just as productivity shortcuts.

Location

Compensation

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $139,370, a midpoint of $199,100, and a maximum salary of $228,965, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop.
